status: research-only negative; no product, release, R4, or canonical-r25 credit
interpretation: The frozen path-blind 4 KiB prefix rule physically reproduces the oracle byte win: 6,134,940 B, 232 B below the accepted v0.29 Analytics artifact.
That density win is economically unusable in the measured complete-create path: median selector creation is 8.5444 s versus 1.5246 s for fresh ZIP/Deflate-9.
The prefix selector is only about 2.56% faster than global L19, far below the predeclared 20% material-speedup alternative gate.

Therefore the result falsifies the current route 'cheap 4 KiB admission probe + L19 on the 45 paying packs' as a practical product solution, without falsifying the underlying observation that high effort can recover Analytics density.
claim_boundary: This is exact-head research evidence on one frozen Analytics workload and a complete-create research surface. It does not establish held-out transfer, canonical r25 integration, 15-workload domination, or release readiness. Thresholds and comparator settings were not changed after measurement.
